Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football Snub against England at 2026 World Cup hurt me – Thomas-Asante Source : Lawrence Degraft Baidoo 20 November 2026 9:39am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ghana international Brandon Thomas-Asante said he was left disappointed in Carlos Queiroz's decision to not use him in the Black Stars' 2026 World Cup game against England.
Having played a key role in Ghana's win over Panama, Thomas-Asante was hoping to star for the Black Stars against the Three Lions.
However, the Portuguese coach had other ideas, opting to leave the Coventry City man on the bench for the entirety of the game, a decision the forward admits was difficult to live with.
"I was thinking this is the game I'm targeting. Like, everything I'm doing is in alignment with performing and showing that I'm one of the best players in the world; that's what I want to do and what I want to be showing.
"And it didn't, of course; it didn't come to pass in that time. I'm sure it hurts. And, you know, it did hurt. It was a hard one to take," he told Joy Sports.
Thomas-Asante also revealed he had approached the former Ghana boss to share his displeasure while urging the coach to trust him more.
“I just had to keep my head down and keep working. As a player, sometimes I feel like I'm coming into my senior years now, so there are conversations that can be had. And I politely said to the manager as well after that game, I think you can trust me more to be a difference-maker on this team.
“And sometimes when you say these things, maybe it's taken well, maybe it's not. But I think, the way I was raised, you go about things as a man, you communicate well, and you're respectful. But you let your opinion; you talk when you need to talk. It was through my desire for wanting to serve the nation and to perform at the World Cup. So, yeah, it was tough,” he added.
The Coventry City man featured in the Black Stars' games against Somalia in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers, where the team picked up six points from both games.
